flight: Use case: stylized-concept. Original hand-inked sprite animation sheet for one heavy air-dropped industrial bomb from a Korean 2D arcade dungeon brawler. Landscape 2:1 canvas. EXACTLY 8 frames on a strict 4-column by 2-row grid; generous margins in EVERY cell and transparent canvas. Every frame shows one and the SAME rigid, large olive-drab cylindrical projectile falling straight down, blunt smoothly hemispherical dark olive nose at BOTTOM, a conspicuously long plain green cylindrical body, a chunky squared gunmetal collar and three short straight stabilizer plates near its TOP, and an exposed flared black engine bell at the TOP. There is ONE broad worn cream identification band and very small amber paint chips. Body height about 3.7 times body width. Orthographic SIDE silhouette, no foreshortening. Heavily outlined, mid-2000s Korean arcade mecha pixel-painted shading in crisp light and shadow clusters, makes a recognizable heavy steel bomb even at 48px wide. Matte steel and enamel. Eight equally scaled drawings, NO BEJEWELED CORE, NO SILVER SPACE POD, NO PURPLE, no glowing body, no sleek pointed nose, no diamond shapes, no hazard symbol or writing, no scenery. Animate ONLY a short yellow-white flame cough and dirty tan exhaust at the top: a few animated frames of puffs, varying in shape under the nozzle; a few vertical motion strokes close to the object. Same anchored nose tip horizontal 50%, vertical 84% within every cell, ~67% cell height is metal, exhaust fits in remaining space. Padding on every side. Original gameplay asset with alpha, no letters, no border, no shadows on ground.
chip: Use case: stylized-concept. Square transparent inventory icon for Reverse Call, Korean mecha action RPG. A premium single front-facing dark brushed gunmetal microchip with gold contact pins and a black enamel inset, entire silhouette contained with margin around all sides. On the inset a SMALL flat graphic badge of a blunt-ended OLIVE GREEN CYLINDER bomb with a black tail cage, descending vertically nose down, with a broad golden-orange mushroom cloud and dusty shock front beneath. Compose as a cohesive readable heraldic relief, restricted color palette olive enamel, ivory stripe and amber. Dark edges, crisp metallic bevel, dramatic painted highlights, item readable at 64x64. No purple, no blue plasma, no text/letters/numerals, no lettering or brands, no scene. Only the object against true transparent alpha.
impactArtDirection: Reference 1 is our game's EXISTING realistic volumetric explosion flipbook, reference 2 is its in-game helicopter bombardment, both for exact VFX material and light-response matching. Create ONE isolated new HERO FRAME of the game's much larger HEAVY QUANTUM BOMB fire-and-smoke plume at peak mass. This output is one single full-color 3D-rendered VFX element on true transparent alpha, not a grid, scene or comparison. Production-quality Houdini pyro / EmberGen film VFX beauty pass with the fidelity of close-up practical pyrotechnics. A heavy white-hot orange-gold center, incandescent dark orange pockets curl deep inside a massive irregular mushroom crown as thick near-black charcoal volumetric smoke rolls OVER the top with rich internal occlusion. Medium-wide natural rising turbulent column, visible negative space beneath overhanging billowing cap on both sides. Natural asymmetric crown, slightly higher on one side, varied smoke features from large billows to frayed thin filaments. Superheated column visually connects a heavy grounded dust skirt to canopy, with some off-axis wisps. Lateral ejection of tawny dust at the feet. A few natural glowing fragments. Oblique game camera sees modest top surfaces of swelling ash, like reference 2; single lower center sole footprint. Distinct readable mass, weight and heat. Central bright areas occupy at most one quarter; charcoal, sienna, rust surround glowing deep orange fissures. RAW PHOTOREALISTIC simulation appearance with continuous values, soft optical falloff, fine volumetric light scattering, detailed midtones, properly fading wispy alpha edges. Absolutely no dark outlines, no hand drawing, no pixel art, no retro arcade textures, no clipart, no idealized symmetric tree, no uniform yellow canopy, no concentric graphic circles, no flat floor, scenery or labels. Square canvas, full tall plume and full ground wave framed with 8% clear margin on every side, the bottom foot lies around 87% of the height.
referenceMaterial: Local V3 battle playback of helicopter airstrike and rocket launcher
plateArtDirection: Edit reference 1, the approved look of our isolated cinematic game pyro plume, into a temporal 3-column x 2-row photorealistic fluid-simulation plate. Reference 2 is our game's existing smaller helicopter strike and is the exact technical/material benchmark: fine hot orange combustion deep inside dense soot, volumetric self-shadow, detailed ash dust, semi-transparent edges. Do NOT put either input sheet or gameplay background into the output. Six distinct sequential frames from ONE continuous simulation for compositing onto an existing video-game arena. Landscape 3:2, uniform invisible grid of three columns and two rows, row major, true transparent RGBA. In every cell camera is locked, balanced same position and scale, ground contact at local x50%, y88%, generous 7% fully clear gutters around each subject. World scale is fixed. Natural asymmetry, right-hand spine slightly taller, left-hand curl lower, wide crown above distinct stalk as in reference 1. Small tan dust skirts on the imaginary ground, no scenic scene/ground plane. No drawn outlines or extreme halos. Rich continuously shaded photographic simulation, not stylization. NO borders, type, glyphs, numbering, comparisons, logos or other objects. The reference is a fully developed image so redraw and evolve the volume with convincing material continuity in each frame. Six genuinely different time samples, not static duplicates. THIS PLATE NEEDS ONLY THE FOLLOWING STAGE:

plateStages.ignition: IGNITION & RAPID ASCENT, frames 1–6 of 24. F1 tiny flat white-orange burst of sparks on the common ground contact (12% of cell), F2 wider ground compression and yellow core ejection (24%), F3 ground dust spreads sideways while a narrow incandescent geyser starts (38%), F4 the upper pocket swells and throws a few dark fragments (48%), F5 fiery stem rises carrying a central turbulent fire mass into the air (59%), F6 a mushroom canopy about 60% cell width has just rounded over on the ascending trunk, overall height 70%. This plate stays luminous yellow-white in center with rich orange turbulent shell, smoke building later. Large clear upper space in early cells. No completed dark mature crown yet.
plateStages.crown: FULL THERMAL BLOOM, frames 7–12 of 24. Every frame shows rapidly churning fire and a common low dust skirt. F7 well-formed fire crown, still more orange than soot, at 65% cell width, 72% height. F8 expands leftwards, F9 fire vents along the lower sides and rivulets of black ash curl around the glowing core; F10 broad mushroom crown and grounded incandescent trunk with granular dark smoke lobes; F11 peak volume like reference 1, filling 82% width and 82% height of the full cell; F12 slightly taller fully rolled roughly asymmetric soot canopy lit underneath. Preserve the brief white-gold fire seen between cracks and the impressive overhangs on BOTH sides of the stalk. Rich inner structure even when shrunk. Low scattering amber dust at the base. No shrink or fade on this plate.
plateStages.cooling: COOLING, frames 13–18 of 24. Begin nearly identical in visual size and overall silhouette to reference 1 (full thermally lit mature wide mushroom cap above column, width and height ~82% of cell). Across six chronologically distinct frames outer smoke rolls outward then curls upward; open orange fissures go from large at first to isolated thin amber cracks, never suddenly disappear. F13/14 right lobe rolls up while low ground dust expands. F15/16 mostly dark brown-charcoal smoke, crest still dense with fine rising gray veils and some deep hot light. F17/18 former stalk begins to detach into ragged convection wisps, cap splits into two broad thinning lobes with fine ivory edges. The last image remains a materially substantial smoky plume about 65% cell width. No initial blinding flash, return to bright yellow, or new explosions.
plateStages.tail: SMOKE DISPERSAL AND EMBERS, frames 19–24 of 24. Six evolving translucent decay shapes on the consistently registered imaginary ground. F19 sprawling soft smoke remnants like the late stages in reference 2: two asymmetric gray-brown rising banks at upper height, broken thin stalk and dusty foot, nearly no visible flame, small red ember speckles. F20 upper smoke expands and thins; F21 crown and stalk shear apart into silver-gray wisps, ground dust fades; F22 just a few independently curling translucent filaments and settling sparks; F23 sparse almost transparent drifting ash at mid-height; F24 only faint vertical gray threads or a few last tiny flecks ABOVE the ground, then nothing. Continuous fade in density as well as shape, no full dark opaque clouds by the last two cells. No new fireball, no upright fully bright mushroom.
